fields.title: Bug 2003214 - Add security audit logger to AI Window security layer r?tarek,#ai-ondevice-reviewers
fields.summary:
Implements console-based security audit logging for policy decisions with:
- Hash.sys.mjs: HMAC-SHA256 hashing with session-scoped throwaway key
  for privacy-preserving logs (per Security Team feedback)
- SecurityLogger.sys.mjs: Console logging with sanitized NDJSON output
- Sensitive fields (URLs, args) hashed before logging
- All policy decisions logged (allow, deny, pref switch bypass, errors)
- Timestamp auto-generated in log() function

fields.title: Bug 2002158 - Avoid throwing exceptions when a crash dump id is missing during tests r=jmaher
Bug 2003190 - Add policy engine to security layer r=tarek,#ai-ondevice-reviewers
fields.summary:
Implements a policy-based security layer for AI Window to protect against
prompt injection attacks. The security layer validates tool execution requests
against a URL ledger that tracks user-authorized URLs.

Key components:
- SecurityOrchestrator: Central coordinator with evaluation flow documentation
- PolicyEvaluator: JSON policy evaluation with "first deny wins" strategy
- ConditionEvaluator: Safe condition evaluation for policy rules
- SecurityLogger: Console-based audit logging (stub for now)
- SecurityUtils: URL normalization, eTLD validation, ledger management
- DecisionTypes: Type definitions and helpers for allow/deny decisions

fields.title: Bug 1940906 - Allow getting a Blob of a model file in the HWInference process, cross-process, without copies. r?#ipc-reviewers
fields.summary:
This is be later used when initializing the speech recognition backend.
The files range from a hundreds megabyte to multiple gigabytes
(depending on the quality and how many languages they can handle), so we
really need to avoid a copy here.

fields.title: Bug 1940906 - Implement the backend for downloading a model file, using ModelHub. r?#ipc-reviewers
fields.summary:
This is very similar to the previous patch (available()), but leverages
the ModelHub to download a model, with progress callback. The download
progress isn't relayed to content (intentionnaly, for fingerprinting
reasons), but a completion callback is (error or success).

Again, this starts in the content process, uses a transient
PSpeechRecognition actor to reach the HWInference process, that asks the
main process (on its main thread) to download a model (or resolve the
promise immediately if already downloaded -- ModelHub implements a
cache).

fields.title: Bug 1940906 - Introduce PSPeechRecognition, implement SpeechRecognition.available(). r?#ipc-reviewers
fields.summary:
SpeechRecognition.available() allows knowing if a particular language is
supported. This patch starts in the content process, instantiate a
SpeechRecognition actor, sending a request to the HWInference process,
that then asks the parent process, at which point the ModelHub can be
queried (on the main thread).

fields.title: Bug 1940906 - Add an XPCOM interface to ModelHub.sys.mjs, add available() to ModelHub. r?tarek,#xpcom-reviewers
fields.summary:
This allows calling into ModelHub from native code. This also adds a
couple testing facilities, and a little bit of formatting fixes.

The testing facilities allow almost end-to-end testing of some
Web Speech API feature, testing all the IPC, but sidestepping the very
last part about having an _actual_ model.

Only the facilities SpeechRecognition needs are exposed via this small
XPCOM component: check availability, download a mode, with progress
callbacks, and getting an fd for a model file stored in ModelHub.

fields.title: Bug 1940906 - Introduce the HWInference utility process. r?#ipc-reviewers,gerard-majax
fields.summary:
The HWInference process is a new type of process, that is created from a
content process (e.g. to implement a Web API), but can also talk to the
main process (e.g. to interact with ModelHub and acquire ML models).

It doesn't run script. It has a dedicated sandbox policy (in a
subsequent patch), that is roughly similar to the GPU process policy,
with everything related to graphics rendering removed (connection to the
display server, access to fonts, misc system calls and privileges,
etc.), as it is just for hardware accelerated computations.

This patch only contains the scaffolding, and the first actor
(PSpeechRecognition) will be introduced in another patch.

Bug 1833332 - Enable stylelint linter against use of px/pt for CSS font-size and line-height. r=gijs,#desktop-theme-reviewers!
fields.summary:
This patch enables stylelint to discourage the use of “px” / “pt” units for `font-size` and `line-height`. The goal is to provide an aid for keeping our `font-size` and `line-height` sizings consistent in Firefox moving forward. 

Follow-up tasks will be filed for the affected modules and the owning teams can decide whether or not to remove `/* stylelint-disable-next-line declaration-property-unit-allowed-list */` from their stylesheets.
